terms.definition: A state of normlessness or breakdown of social norms associated with strain and disconnection.
The physical act component of an offense (conceptual).
The mental state element (intent/knowledge/recklessness/negligence) depending on offense.
Prevention via perceived certainty, swiftness, and proportionality of consequence.
Crime as convergence of motivated offender, suitable target, and absent guardian.
Theory that crime is learned through social interactions and definitions favorable to law violation.
Independent support for a claim from separate sources.
Over-commitment to one hypothesis while ignoring alternatives.
Study of victimization patterns and impacts, emphasizing prevention without blame.
Pressure, opportunity, rationalization as common conditions in fraud contexts.
Area with concentrated incidents due to opportunity and routine patterns.
Functional method used to accomplish an act; may evolve over time.
Expressive elements beyond function (use cautiously; requires corroboration).
